messages:
sasha: Heads-up — hitting weird typing errors in rust-sdk when using function/tool calling with structured outputs. Model often wraps the payload in an envelope like {"kind":"result", "payload": {...}} but our Deserialize expects the payload root. Any recommended SDK helpers or patterns?

jamal: Oh yeah we've seen that. Can you paste the exact model output + your expected struct?

sasha: Sure. Minimal repro:
```rust
#[derive(serde::Deserialize, Debug)]
struct Action { command: String, args: Vec<String> }

// model response (string):
// {"kind":"result","payload":{"command":"ls","args":["-la"]}}
// attempted: serde_json::from_str::<Action>(&resp) -> Err
```

claire: Two things: (1) envelope mismatch (as you said) and (2) streaming chunking — sometimes the JSON arrives in pieces so immediate parse fails. For the envelope you can either use an enum with a wrapper or a small coercion middleware in the SDK that unwraps known envelopes.

jamal: Example pattern we used in TS: return union type Result<T, RawValue> so callers can fall back to raw JSON. For Rust: something like
```rust
#[derive(Deserialize)]
#[serde(untagged)]
enum MaybeEnvelope<T> {
  Direct(T),
  Envelope { kind: String, payload: T }
}
// then: let out: MaybeEnvelope<Action> = serde_json::from_str(&s)?;
```
That keeps things explicit and avoids data loss.

sasha: That helps but it's clunky to repeat for every tool. Would love an SDK helper macro or wrapper to generate these boilerplate enums/impls. Also want the SDK to optionally store the raw Value for tracing/audit.

nik: I can add a helper in rust-sdk: `#[derive(FunctionOutput)]` or `redwood_sdk::func::coerce_envelope::<T>()` which returns `Result<T, serde_json::Value>` and optionally logs the raw. Also will add a streaming-safe parser that buffers tokens until a full JSON value is seen before deserializing.

sasha: Streaming-safe parser is critical. We've observed model streaming split the envelope start in one event and the payload in the next, causing early parse errors inside tokio streams. Any suggested approach?

claire: Accumulate bytes until serde_json::from_slice succeeds. For performance, cap buffer size and cut to raw Value if oversized. Another approach: parse with a streaming parser (serde_json::Deserializer::from_slice) and call into Value when complete.

jamal: Proposed SDK API sketch: `call_function(..., coerce: CoerceMode)` where CoerceMode = { None, Envelope(String /*field*/), KeepRaw }. Default None for strictness, Envelope unwraps if the named key exists.

nik: I'll prototype `CoerceMode::Envelope("payload")` + derive macro that implements TryFrom<Value> for your typed struct so the SDK can return T directly when it matches, else Raw(Value). Will add feature flag so teams opt-in.

sasha: Would prefer default runtime shape: `Result<T, serde_json::Value>` rather than panic/deserial-error. That makes rollbacks and audits easy.

ci-bot: CI: rust-unit-tests #482 passed on branch feat/rust-func-coerce (3/3) :white_check_mark:

jamal: Also add an integration test that simulates chunked streaming (send `{"kind":"res` then `ult","payload":{...}}`) so we don't regress.

claire: Note: document perf tradeoffs — extra parse step per call. Make it configurable.

sasha: Awesome. Nik — want me to open a PR with a small RFC + tests? I'll include example macros and streamed parser tests.

nik: Please do. Assign to me for review. @sasha :thumbsup:
